events.title: Ruby on Rails 7.0 released
events.summary: Rails 7.0 shipped on December 15, 2021 with import maps, Hotwire (Turbo + Stimulus), and encrypted attributes by default.
events.about: Rails 7 answered the JavaScript framework question: ship modern interactivity without Node bundlers via import maps and Turbo Drive. Encrypted columns and async query loading kept Rails competitive for SaaS APIs and monoliths that wanted React-level UX with Ruby ergonomics.

narrative.whyChosen: Rails 7 defined the no-Node-default path for full-stack Ruby web apps.
narrative.whyImportant: Import maps and Hotwire reduced JavaScript toolchain complexity for Rails teams.
narrative.problemSolved: Rails apps felt forced into webpack/React complexity to match SPA expectations.

events.title: Django 4.0 released
events.summary: The Django team released Django 4.0 on December 7, 2021 with `zoneinfo` timezone support, `scrypt` password hashing, and Redis cache backend.
events.about: Django 4 dropped Python 3.6 support and modernized defaults: stdlib timezones replaced pytz; scrypt strengthened password storage; Redis became a built-in cache option. It powered admin panels, REST APIs, and CMS backends through the early 2020s.

narrative.whyChosen: Django 4 was the Python 3-only cleanup that aligned with modern deployment practices.
narrative.whyImportant: Built-in Redis caching and zoneinfo simplified production Django stacks.
narrative.problemSolved: Django carried pytz and legacy compatibility baggage from the Python 2 era.

events.title: Log4Shell vulnerability disclosed
events.summary: Apache disclosed CVE-2021-44228 on December 9, 2021 — Log4Shell, a critical remote code execution flaw in the ubiquitous Log4j logging library.
events.about: A crafted JNDI lookup string in log messages could execute arbitrary code on millions of Java servers — Minecraft, enterprise apps, and cloud services scrambled to patch over the holidays. Log4Shell became the benchmark for dependency-scanning, runtime WAF rules, and the phrase 'it's always logging' in security memes.

narrative.whyChosen: Log4Shell was the most severe open-source supply-chain bug since Heartbleed.
narrative.whyImportant: It made software composition analysis and emergency patching mandatory for Java shops.
narrative.problemSolved: Nothing until upgraded — any app logging attacker-controlled strings was remotely exploitable.
